content.value_statement: LLM applications can become difficult to structure as agents, memory, retrieval, and tools grow. This skill guides LangChain design choices and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains LangChain agents, chains, memory, document processing, and callbacks.
Provides architecture patterns for RAG, custom tools, and multi-step workflows.
Shows how to choose memory strategies for different conversation lengths.
Outlines callback use for logging, monitoring, and debugging.
Includes testing, performance, and production readiness guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a maintained LangChain package.
Examples may need updates for current LangChain API versions.
It does not validate security controls for real external tools or APIs.
It does not replace production testing, monitoring, or threat modeling.

use_cases.title: Plan a RAG Assistant
use_cases.description: Design document loading, chunking, vector storage, retrieval, and source return behavior for a knowledge assistant.

use_cases.title: Structure Agent Tools
use_cases.description: Define agent tool boundaries, descriptions, memory behavior, and execution checks before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess error handling, callbacks, token monitoring, rate limits, testing, and fallback behavior for a LangChain workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a LangChain app for [goal]. Compare agent, chain, and RAG patterns. Recommend one design and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LangChain RAG workflow for [document type]. Include loaders, chunking, embeddings, vector store choice, retrieval settings, and source handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Memory and Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture for an agent that uses [tools] and remembers [context]. Define memory type, tool descriptions, guardrails, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LangChain architecture for production. Check observability, testing, latency, cost, retries, rate limits, input validation, and security risks.

output_examples.input: Design a customer support RAG assistant for product manuals.
output: Recommended pattern: retrieval augmented generation with source documents returned.
Core components: document loader, text splitter, embeddings, vector store, retriever, and answer chain.
Production checks: source visibility, stale document handling, token limits, and retrieval quality tests.

output_examples.input: Choose memory for a long-running chat assistant.
output: Use summary memory for older context and window memory for recent turns.
Track important entities separately when user preferences or account details matter.
Add tests for context drift, privacy boundaries, and maximum prompt length.

output_examples.input: Review an agent with search and email tools.
output: Separate read-only search tools from tools that cause external actions.
Require confirmation before sending messages or making irreversible changes.
Log tool calls, failures, token usage, and user approval decisions.

best_practices: Start with the simplest chain or RAG pattern before adding autonomous agent behavior.
Write clear tool descriptions and enforce validation around action-capable tools.
Add callbacks, tests, rate limits, timeouts, and cost monitoring before production use.
anti_patterns: Giving an agent broad tool access without approvals or execution limits.
Using unbounded conversation memory until the context window becomes unreliable.
Shipping retrieval without checking chunk quality, source accuracy, and stale data handling.

faq.question: What does this skill help me design?
faq.answer: It helps design LangChain applications with agents, chains, memory, retrieval, callbacks, testing, and production checks.

faq.question: Does it generate a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and examples that you adapt to your codebase and current LangChain version.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it focused only on RAG?
faq.answer: No. It also covers agents, sequential chains, memory strategies, callbacks, testing, and performance patterns.

faq.question: What should I verify before production?
faq.answer: Verify error handling, input validation, rate limits, token costs, observability, tool approvals, and retrieval accuracy.

faq.question: Are the examples version specific?
faq.answer: The examples are conceptual and may require API updates for the LangChain version used in your project.
